items.article_search_text: Oscar Piastri has made a damning admission about driving the 2026 Formula 1 cars, stating that the AI reduces his Oscar Piastri has made a damning admission about driving the 2026 F1 cars, stating that the AI reduces his input at points when out on track. Motorsport Week is an independent, FIA accredited motorsport website delivering the latest Formula 1, Formula E, GP2, GP3, WEC, IndyCar, Nascar, Formula 3, WRC, WRX, DTM, IMSA and MotoGP news and results. Oscar Piastri has made a damning admission about driving the 2026 Formula 1 cars, stating that the AI reduces his input at points when out on track. Piastri is enduring a challenging season, struggling to get to grips with the new generation of car, yet to win a race in 2026. The Australian has been one of the more quieter drivers in giving his verdict on the cars, which feature a near 50:50 split in electrical and internal combustion power. But he has made an damning admission over the computer systems onboard the cars, which actively learns the circuit and how to deploy the battery during a lap. "Sometimes, yes," Piastri said to media, including Motorsport Week, if he "felt like a passenger of the AI systems". "At a track like Spa or a track like Silverstone, it’s going to be worse. At the Hungaroring or Zandvoort, I really don’t expect there to be many problems at all with that kind of thing, because the straights are so much shorter, so even if there are differences, they should be a lot less. "But the principle of driving a race car that loses effectively half of its power before the end of the straight is hard to get your head around sometimes. Oscar Piastri has made a damning admission over the AI in the current generation of F1 cars Oscar Piastri details AI issues Elaborating on his point, Piastri detailed the radical way the car learns the sectors of the legendary Spa circuit. "Even in Spa, a lot of the middle sector we were doing it just on the combustion engine, with no battery assistance at all, which is a weird feeling in itself, having some corners with a certain amount of power and others with full power. "I think Spa was particularly frustrating, not just for me but for quite a lot of others, because those small differences in the code and what the engines did made quite a big difference in lap time. "Especially at the front of the field, I think there were still only nine hundredths or something separating four positions, and there were definitely more than nine hundredths on the table for quite a few drivers from things they could not control." Piastri's feedback on the car's AI systems highlights the journey F1 faces with these regulations. For a driver to feel like a passenger is not a sentiment many will want to experience. items.article_search_text: McLaren F1 star Oscar Piastri teamed up with Kevin Pietersen on The Switch to showcase his cricket skills against a 100 mph bowling machine. have i ever watched a cricket game before? no do i know any cricket rules? Oscar Piastri playing cricket wasn’t on anyone’s bingo card. In a surprising crossover that has fans talking, the McLaren Formula 1 driver recently traded the racetrack for the crease.The Australian star took on a high-speed cricket challenge on his YouTube series, The Switch, hosted by former England batsman Kevin Pietersen. Filmed around mid-August 2026, the off-track session used a bowling machine to push deliveries up toward the 100mph mark just for fun.Now, F1 fans are left wondering if he can actually play the game and how he managed to handle those intense deliveries. Let's see exactly what went down!Piastri is still fully committed to McLaren and his Formula 1 career. The cricket session was just a fun, light-hearted guest appearance on Kevin Pietersen’s YouTube series, , reportedly per .Reports confirm that it was strictly a one-off challenge with a bowling machine, rather than any sort of career change or exit from the F1 grid. The McLaren driver is still racing in the 2026 season with his usual car number, 81.The Melbourne-born driver actually grew up playing junior cricket, mostly as a bowler, along with Australian Rules football before he shifted his focus entirely to karting and racing.He’s often spoken about his genuine love for the game, reportedly even heading out to watch matches like the Melbourne Test, and is good friends with players like Mitchell Starc. During the challenge, he took on deliveries from a bowling machine that started at 51 mph, playing with three “lives” as the speed progressively cranked up.Piastri managed to handle deliveries all the way up to 81 mph. Starting at 51 mph and using his three allotted lives, he steadily worked his way through the different speeds on the bowling machine, reportedly reaching 81 mph at his final attempt.That final 81 mph figure happened to perfectly match his Formula 1 race number, adding a fun coincidence to the session. Even though he didn't quite hit the maximum 100 mph target, it was still a really impressive performance for someone who isn't a professional cricketer.Clocking in at 81 mph actually puts Piastri second on challenge leaderboard. The ranking reportedly has Bollywood actor Suniel Shetty holding onto the top spot with a higher speed of around 91 to 92 mph, while tennis star Andy Murray finished just behind at 79 mph.This places the F1 driver ahead of quite a few other high-profile guests who have taken on the exact same progressive speed bowling machine test.One user on Reddit wrote, “First we had Max vs 100 drivers. Now it's Oscar vs 100 mph ball. Wonder what's next for the vs 100 series.”Another mentioned, “His first instinct is to go defensive. That's how you know he's an Aussie batter.” A third joked, “I laughed so hard when he left the ball.” Another added, “Australian player defaults to Test match mode, as per usual.”For Piastri, the cricket challenge was another reminder that his sporting talent stretches far beyond the Formula 1 circuit.

items.article_search_text: The McLaren boss attributes the Australian's lack of pace to excessive reflection behind the wheel of the MCL40. The team has designed a plan for him to recover his fluency and fight for the podium again in the final stretch of the season. Andrea Stella has identified the source of Oscar Piastri [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/oscar-piastri-describes-spanish-gp-as-painful-after-challenging-f1-outing]'s problems. The McLaren boss considers that the Australian driver is "thinking too much" while driving the MCL40, which prevents him from extracting the full potential of the car and is costing him valuable tenths in qualifying and races: "I think with Oscar we need to qualify better and be closer to the podium positions from the start, there are several circumstances over which we need more control. We need to execute the work better and at the same time achieve greater synchrony between Oscar and the MCL40, since he still drives thinking too much" declared Stella in Madrid. The Italian executive's diagnosis points to an adaptation problem. Piastri, who in 2025 had stood out for his ability to maintain great speed in fast corners, has not been able to consistently reproduce that style with the current generation of cars, the reduction in downforce and narrower tires have altered the behavior of the cars, reducing available grip and demanding a different driving approach. Oscar Piastri describes Spanish GP as “painful” after challenging F1 outing [https://deweb-519a7.b-cdn.net/post-images/60f26e36-1416-4168-8752-9508c5914746.jpeg] Oscar Piastri describes Spanish GP as “painful” after challenging F1 outing The Australian finished eighth after suffering front wing damage on the first lap from contact with Russell. The bad timing of the Virtual Safety Car and a complicated qualifying session hampered his race at Madring. [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/oscar-piastri-describes-spanish-gp-as-painful-after-challenging-f1-outing] For Piastri that adaptation process is proving slower than expected, Stella explained how this excess reflection directly affects performance: "When you drive thinking too much everything becomes slower, you become slower as a driver when deciding what to do and consequently, you do slower laps" he noted. The McLaren [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/mclaren]boss trusts that the team can reverse the situation. "The plan is very clear in terms of what we need to improve and I hope we get past this seeing a stronger Piastri in the final part of the year" he added. The Monza case is a representative example of Piastri's season, the Australian qualified third but a penalty for impeding another driver dropped him to sixth place on the grid, ruining his podium chances: "In Monza, he was third in qualifying but we ended up starting sixth due to a penalty. There are several circumstances over which we need more control" lamented Stella. F1 Stock Watch: Who Gained and Lost More After Madrid? [https://deweb-519a7.b-cdn.net/post-images/b429bb20-8779-402e-811d-c0b69c9373bc.jpeg] F1 Stock Watch: Who Gained and Lost More After Madrid? Kimi Antonelli's stock is through the roof, while Carlos Sainz Jr's hometown flop will hurt him. [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/f1-stock-watch-who-gained-and-lost-more-after-madrid] The figures reflect the gap between McLaren's two drivers, Piastri has 120 points and occupies seventh place in the championship, with two podiums and no wins. Lando Norris, for his part, is fourth with 186 points, two wins and five podiums. The 66 point difference between them is a reflection of the Australian's lack of consistency, who has not managed to find the consistency needed to fight for the title. McLaren has established a strategy to recover Piastri's performance in the second half of the season. The goal is to achieve greater synchrony between the driver and the car so that Piastri can drive more instinctively and less analytically, the team trusts that with more adaptation time and specific work on the MCL40's setup, the Australian can recover the fluency that led him to shine in previous seasons. Formula 1 [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1] will return to action in Baku, where Piastri will have a new opportunity to demonstrate that McLaren's recovery plan is producing results. The Australian knows time is pressing and that every race is a chance to recover the confidence and pace that made him one of the most promising drivers on the grid.

Outside of her professional life, she enjoys exploring new music and travelling. category: general news Oscar Piastri’s journey from junior motorsport in Melbourne to Formula One has involved success across multiple racing categories. After progressing through karting and winning several junior championships, Piastri joined McLaren and became a Formula One race winner. His career reflects the importance of driver development, competitive results and support throughout the early stages of a motorsport career. A Melbourne beginning in motorsport Piastri was born in Melbourne in 2001 and developed an interest in motorsport from a young age. He began with radio-controlled racing before moving into karting at the age of ten. During his karting years, he competed in junior events and won regional championships. His father, Chris Piastri, supported his early racing career, including involvement with his karting activities. Like many young motorsport competitors, Piastri’s progression required significant investment, travel and support as he moved through increasingly competitive racing categories. Success through junior racing categories Piastri built his reputation through success in European junior motorsport. He won the Formula Renault Eurocup championship in 2019, followed by the FIA Formula 3 Championship in 2020 and the FIA Formula 2 Championship in 2021. Winning championships across these categories helped establish him as a leading young driver and positioned him for opportunities in Formula One. However, success in junior categories does not automatically guarantee a Formula One seat, as teams consider factors including performance, timing, sponsorship and available opportunities. Entering Formula One with McLaren After involvement with a Formula One driver development program, Piastri joined McLaren for the 2023 season. He made his Formula One debut at the 2023 Bahrain Grand Prix and achieved his first podium finish later that year at the Japanese Grand Prix. In 2024, Piastri won his first Formula One race at the Hungarian Grand Prix and later added another victory at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix. These results made him the fifth Australian driver to win a Formula One race. Competing at the highest level Piastri continued achieving strong results with McLaren as his Formula One career developed. During the 2025 season, he recorded additional race victories and competed near the front of the championship standings. His early Formula One career has included race wins, podium finishes and competition for leading positions within the sport. He remains contracted with McLaren, continuing his development as a Formula One driver. The financial side of Formula One Formula One drivers at leading teams can earn income through team contracts, sponsorship agreements and commercial partnerships. As with other professional athletes, estimates of Piastri’s Wealth are based on external assessments of earnings, endorsements and other financial interests rather than publicly audited personal financial statements. Driver Earnings can change significantly depending on contracts, results and commercial opportunities. Driving style and development Piastri has been recognised for his measured approach to racing and ability to manage pressure. Formula One requires drivers to combine technical skill, physical preparation, decision-making and consistency across long race weekends. His progression through multiple racing categories provided experience in different cars, circuits and competitive environments before reaching Formula One. An Australian presence in Formula One Piastri’s career continues Australia’s involvement in Formula One. Australian drivers have competed successfully in the championship, including world champions and race winners who have represented the country internationally. Piastri’s arrival at McLaren has increased Australian interest in Formula One and added another driver to the country’s representation in the sport. The career journey Oscar Piastri’s career demonstrates the progression required to reach Formula One. His pathway involved years of karting, success in junior championships and adaptation to the demands of professional racing. The move from junior categories to Formula One requires both performance and opportunity, and Piastri’s early results have established him as one of Australia’s current Formula One competitors.
